claim: N02's rule that "An error is thrown if the file does not exist" does not hold when --env-file-if-exists is used instead, a flag that N03 says was only Added in: v22.9.0.
would_change: Turns "a missing env file always aborts Node" into "it aborts only with --env-file; on v22.9.0+ use --env-file-if-exists for optional files" — and on runtimes older than v22.9.0 there is no documented flag-level escape, so the caller must guard the file's existence outside Node.

claim: N06 (v22.5.1) documents node:sqlite as reachable only by passing --experimental-sqlite (Added in: v22.5.0), while N07 (v22.20.0) records "v22.13.0 SQLite is unflagged but still experimental" and documents only --no-experimental-sqlite to disable it.
would_change: Changes "you must pass --experimental-sqlite to use node:sqlite" to "only on v22.5.0–v22.12.x; from v22.13.0 the module is on by default and the flag you may need is --no-experimental-sqlite." These are different Node versions, so this is a default flip across versions, not a contradiction.

claim: N11 is titled "fs.watch() Caveats: recursive restriction removed" but its excerpt contains no sentence about the recursive option at all — the removal is inferred from absence relative to N10.
would_change: Downgrades "v20.19.0 docs state the recursive restriction was lifted" to "the v20.19.0 Caveats excerpt simply omits the restriction sentence present in v18.20.4"; anyone relying on recursive:true on Linux needs the actual fs.watch option documentation or a runtime check, not this excerpt.

claim: The excerpts do not say whether fs.watch({recursive:true}) is supported on Linux, BSD, or SunOS in v20.19.0; N11 lists per-platform notification mechanisms (inotify, kqueue, FSEvents, event ports, ReadDirectoryChangesW) without tying any of them to the recursive option, and N10 states ERR_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE_ON_PLATFORM is thrown on unsupported platforms.
would_change: Decides whether cross-platform watcher code targeting Node 20 can drop its macOS/Windows-only guard and its ERR_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE_ON_PLATFORM handling, or must keep them.

claim: Quote stripping, multi-line value syntax, and the ignored export keyword are documented only in N04 (v24.8.0); N02 (v22.20.0) states none of them and records only the history line "v21.7.0, v20.12.0 Add support to multi-line values."
would_change: Leaves open whether a .env file using backtick/quote delimiters or `export KEY=...` parses identically on v22.20.0; multi-line is implied supported by the v21.7.0/v20.12.0 history line, but quote-stripping and export-keyword handling are unverified for v22. The screen's "exception" label for this pair is wrong — the two excerpts describe complementary aspects of the same flag and assert nothing incompatible.
